title: Hinton explains the oral history project's purpose
summary: Hinton explains that the Smithsonian wants family background so future generations know the jazz pioneers; Leeman says family shaped him as a drummer.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: The reason for this is we're doing this for the Smithsonian Institute, and this is what we call Oral History, so that young people and people in America and throughout the world will know about great artists like you who have made a name, who have gone through and made a name for themselves in jazz and have been the pioneers of jazz, and you and guys like you -- and you certainly are one of the pioneers of this great American art form known as jazz.

So we're trying to do this so that long after we're gone, they will know about you and they will know what you did and the accomplishments that you did and hear in your own voice how you felt about your era and what happened. So it is very important that we know about your family and where you came from and what it was like. Is that clear as to what we're trying to do?
Because they had a great deal of influence on how I turned out to be a drummer.
Right, right. So we want to get that.
